01.r: Strengthens the command: the tithe is to be given in full.
01.n: The verb is doubled: an infinitive of 'tithe' stands before the finite verb, a Hebrew way of stressing it. Our 'surely' renders this first form. The Geneva and DRC do not render it.

s: you shall give a tenth of
you shall set aside a tenth of
02.r: Each Israelite is to give a tenth of what his fields produce.
02.n: The brief's lexicon gives this stem the sense 'to give a tithe'. Gesenius: PIEL, to give the tenth part, and he cites this verse for the thing tithed as the object. The 'you' is singular, addressed to each Israelite.
t: Thou shalt giue the tithe of
thou shalt set aside the tithes of
You must ... set aside a tenth of

03.r: Marks what follows as the thing tithed.
03.n: The object marker has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'all'.

04.r: None of the produce is left out.

05.r: What the land yields from what was sown.
05.n: Gesenius: produce, as of the earth; BDB: product, revenue. The older English versions say 'increase'.

06.r: The grain and crops you have sown.
06.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as sowing, and then seed. The DRC and BSB do not render the word.

07.r: What grows up out of the field.
07.n: A participle with the article, 'the one coming out'. Hebrew has no 'of' here: the field follows the verb directly. Most translations turn it round to 'that the field brings forth'.
t: that which is brought forth in

08.n: The DRC says 'the earth', the BSB 'your fields'.

09.r: The tithe is due every year.
09.n: Gesenius cites this verse for the doubled form 'year year', meaning yearly.

10.n: Hebrew simply repeats the word, 'year year'; English needs 'by'.

02.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. ἀποδεκατόω, 'tithe, take a tenth', the verb used for tithing in the New Testament.

05.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives θνησιμαῖος, which is wrong here. γένημα means produce.

06.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none.

07.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. The Greek says 'the produce of your field' where the Hebrew says 'that comes out of the field'.

08.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. The Greek adds 'your'.

10.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives αὐτός, which is wrong here. ἐνιαυτὸν κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν, 'year by year'.
